# March 2025 Revenue Crisis Analysis

## Summary
Revenue collapsed 56.8% in March 2025, dropping from $1.37M in February to $590K—the lowest monthly performance in the 15-month dataset. Order volume fell 51.6% while customer count dropped to just 96 unique buyers. The crisis was broad-based, affecting all customer segments and geographic regions, with rapid recovery beginning in April 2025.

## Key Findings

• **Massive revenue drop**: March 2025 revenue of $590,243 was 56.8% below February's $1,367,550
• **Order volume collapsed**: Only 108 completed orders versus 223 in February (-51.6%)
• **Customer base contracted**: Unique customers fell from 183 to 96 (-47.5%)
• **All segments affected**: SMB hit hardest with 61.2% revenue drop, followed by Startups (-61.7%) and Enterprise (-40.8%)
• **Rapid recovery**: April revenue rebounded 129.6% to $1.35M, returning to normal levels
• **Average order value stable**: Remained around $5,465 in March, indicating pricing wasn't the issue

## Detail

### Revenue Performance
March 2025 represented the worst monthly performance in the entire dataset, with revenue dropping to levels not seen before or since. The $590,243 total was approximately half the typical monthly range of $1.3-1.6M. See march_2025_revenue_crisis.png for the complete trend visualization.

### Segment Impact Analysis
Every customer segment experienced significant declines, but smaller businesses were disproportionately affected:

- **SMB**: Orders fell from 102 to 49 (-52.0%), revenue dropped 61.2% to $240,748
- **Startup**: Orders fell from 73 to 31 (-57.5%), revenue dropped 61.7% to $169,238  
- **Enterprise**: Orders fell from 48 to 28 (-41.7%), revenue dropped 40.8% to $180,257

Enterprise customers showed the most resilience, suggesting the crisis may have been related to economic uncertainty affecting smaller businesses more severely. See segment_impact_march_2025.png for the visual comparison.

### Geographic Distribution
The impact was geographically widespread, affecting all major markets:
- France: 18 orders ($104,535 revenue)
- Germany: 19 orders ($86,484 revenue)  
- Netherlands: 15 orders ($70,999 revenue)
- Poland: 37 orders ($212,686 revenue)
- UK: 19 orders ($115,540 revenue)

### Daily Patterns
March showed consistently low daily performance with an average of just 3.5 orders and $19,040 revenue per day. The peak day (March 9) generated only $36,758, while the lowest day (March 4) produced just $5,394.

### Product Categories
All product categories were affected proportionally:
- Consulting: $294,276 → $105,209 (-64.3%)
- SaaS: $348,460 → $108,034 (-69.0%)
- Support: $510,248 → $376,999 (-26.1%)

## Caveats

The data does not reveal the root cause of the March 2025 crisis. Several potential explanations could account for this pattern:

• **External economic shock**: Market disruption, financial crisis, or industry-specific event
• **Operational issues**: System outages, sales team disruption, or process breakdowns  
• **Competitive pressure**: Major competitor launch or aggressive pricing
• **Seasonal factors**: Though this seems unlikely given the magnitude and isolation of the event
• **Data quality issues**: Potential recording or processing errors, though the recovery pattern suggests real business impact

The uniform impact across all segments, geographies, and product categories suggests a systemic rather than targeted issue. The rapid recovery in April indicates the underlying business fundamentals remained strong.
